AIR INTELLIGENCE REQUIREMENTS
MEMORANDUM NUMBER 4


                        UNCONVENTIONAL AIRCRAFT

                            PART I - GENERAL

1.  PURPOSE

    本メモランダムの目的は二点である:

    a.  いわゆる「飛行円盤」を含む、非定型航空機および未確認飛行物体の目撃に関する情報に対する空軍の継続的要求事項を明示すること。

    b.  そのような情報を報告するための手順を確立すること。

2.  RESCISSION

    軍務省（Department of the Army）収集メモランダム第7号（1948年1月21日付）および書簡 CSGID 425.1（1948年3月25日付）、いずれも上記主題に属し、空軍機関に措置のため移管されたものは、本書により代替される。

3.  REPORTING

    a.  一般

        (1)  第II部で示される要求に対するできる限り完全な回答は、目撃直後に電信によって直ちに送信されるべきである。

        (2)  補足報告は、報告された情報の重要性に一致する最も迅速な手段により入手次第送付されるべきである。

    b.  Major Air Commands (Overseas) and Air Attaches

        (1)  初報および補足の電報は、Headquarters United States Air Force, Director of Intelligence宛に送信される。電報には句「Pass to COMGENAMC WRIGHT-PATTERSON AFB, DAYTON, OHIO, ATTN: MCIAXO-3.」を含めること。

(1) Reports will be forwarded direct to the Commanding General, Air Materiel Command, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Dayton, Ohio, Attn: MCIAXO-3 by installations receiving information pertaining to the requirements enunciated in Part II.

(2) Copies of such reports may be supplied the Command Headquarters of the installation concerned.

(3) A copy of all reports sent to Air Materiel Command in accordance with these instructions will be forwarded at the same time to the Director of Intelligence, Headquarters United States Air Force.

(4) Written reports will be submitted on AF Form 112.

(5) Commanding General, Air Materiel Command is authorized direct contact with major Air Commands (ZI) and organizations under their control in connection with the development of information on this subject.

(1) Addressees other than those of the United States Air Force are requested to forward reports direct to the Commanding General, Air Materiel Command, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Dayton, Ohio, Attn: MCIAXO-3.

2. Time of sighting (zonal by 24 hr. clock).

      (3) From building (story), yard, etc.

      (4) Map coordinates (if feasible) showing latitude and longitude.

If radius of turn is not observable, how long did the target stay in the turn and what was its speed?

4. Possible releases of testing devices in vicinity sent aloft by Ordnance, Navy, Air Force, Army, Weather Units, Research Organizations or any other.

5. If object contacted earth, obtain soil samples within and without depression or spot where object landed (and then presumably departed) for purpose of making comparison of soils.

summaryEn: Air Intelligence Requirements Memorandum No. 4 dated 15 February 1949 from the USAF Directorate of Intelligence concerning "Unconventional Aircraft" (including so-called flying discs). Purpose: (1) state ongoing Air Force requirements for information on sightings of unconventional/unidentified flying objects, and (2) establish reporting procedures. The memo mandates immediate electrical transmission of initial reports, prompt supplementary reports, and written reports on AF Form 112; cables are to be sent to the Director of Intelligence, HQ USAF, with instructions to pass to COMGENAMC Wright-Patterson AFB (Attn: MCIAXO-3). It authorizes the Commanding General, Air Materiel Command, direct contact with major commands and prescribes reporting responsibilities for overseas commands and non-Air-Force agencies. Part II enumerates required report items: date/time, observer position (ground/air/sea) with coordinates, number/formation, possible celestial explanations, distance/angle/altitude, time in sight, detailed appearance (color, shape, construction, size), direction, maneuvers, exhaust/cloud/light effects, support/propulsion/control features, air ducts, speed, sound, manner of disappearance; observer identity, occupation, hobbies, reliability and witness/interrogator notes; radar-specific observations. Additional instructions cover local weather/winds aloft, nearby flight schedules, possible test releases, soil sampling if landed, Geiger checks, photographs/sketches, signed statements, recovery of fragments, and noting any antenna-like projections. Signed by Major General C. P. Cabell, Director of Intelligence; distribution list includes major Air Commands, US air attaches, DCI, Navy/Coast Guard intelligence, State Department research assistant, and the FBI.
